If only given encrypted HTTPS traffic and ancillary services like DNS, they couldn't tell he looked specifically at FPH. They could potentially tell by DNS records that there was a lookup for voat.co, but what content was requested under voat.co is opaque. What pages you request are encrypted.

GET /v/fatpeoplehate
Host: voat.co
User-Agent: some-browser
Accept: text/html
... more headers

With the traffic encrypted via HTTPS, these just appear as random bytes sent to an IP address that resolves to voat.co.
